title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
plain: The computer is seeing misfires in more than one cylinder, or in cylinders that keep changing. If the check engine light is flashing, ease off and stop driving soon, because a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter.
symptoms: Check engine light on, and it may flash during a heavy misfire
Rough or shaky idle
Stumbling, jerking or loss of power when accelerating
Worse fuel economy and possibly a fuel or rotten-egg smell

causes.name: Worn-out spark plugs
Vacuum leak from a cracked hose or intake gasket
Weak or failing ignition coils or plug wires
Low fuel pressure from a weak pump or clogged filter
Dirty mass airflow sensor or other lean condition
Bad gas, low compression or a jumped timing belt or chain

checks: Look for other codes (lean codes, single-cylinder misfire codes) that point to the real cause
Check when the spark plugs were last replaced and inspect them
Listen and check for vacuum leaks, and check fuel pressure
fix: Most often a set of spark plugs (and any weak coils); if that doesn't cure it, the shop moves on to vacuum leaks, fuel pressure and compression.
examples: Very common on high-mileage engines still running old or original spark plugs
Cracked intake or PCV hoses on older trucks and SUVs often trigger it
drive: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine shakes hard, slow down and get it checked right away; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter. If the light is steady and it runs only a little rough, drive gently to a shop within a few days.
test_first: Look for other codes, then check plugs, coils, vacuum leaks and fuel pressure, and compression or timing if needed. Random misfires often share one cause, so find it before replacing parts.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing, or the engine is shaking hard or losing power: ease off the gas, avoid hard acceleration and heavy loads, and get off the road and have it checked right away. Driving on a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and can leave you without power in traffic.

title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
plain: The computer noticed that cylinder 1 isn't firing properly, so it isn't adding its share of power. If the check engine light is flashing, ease off and stop driving soon, because unburned fuel can overheat the catalytic converter.
symptoms: Check engine light on, and it may flash while the misfire is happening
Rough or shaky idle
Hesitation or stumble when accelerating
Less power and worse fuel economy

causes.name: Worn or fouled spark plug in cylinder 1
Failing ignition coil or plug wire for cylinder 1
Clogged or leaking fuel injector for cylinder 1
Vacuum leak near that cylinder's intake port
Low compression from a burnt valve, worn rings or head gasket problem

checks: Pull the spark plug for that cylinder and look for wear, oil or carbon
Swap the coil with a neighboring cylinder and see if the misfire moves with it
Run a compression test if plugs and coils check out
fix: Usually a new spark plug and/or ignition coil for that cylinder; if the misfire stays put after those, check the injector and compression.

cost.job: Replace spark plug and ignition coil (one cylinder)

drive: If the check engine light flashes or the engine shakes badly, ease off and get it checked right away; unburned fuel from a misfiring cylinder can overheat the catalytic converter. If the light is steady and it runs mostly smooth, drive gently to a shop within a few days.
test_first: Inspect cylinder 1's plug, swap its coil with a neighbor to see if the misfire follows, check its injector, and run a compression test if those check out, before replacing parts.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing, or the engine is shaking hard or losing power: ease off the gas, avoid hard acceleration and heavy loads, and get off the road and have it checked right away. Driving on a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and can leave you without power in traffic.

title: Misfire Detected with Low Fuel
plain: The engine misfired while the fuel tank was very low. Running close to empty can let the pump suck air or overheat, which starves the engine of fuel.
symptoms: Check engine light on after running low on fuel
Stumbling or jerking, especially on turns or hills
Engine may stall or sputter

causes.name: Fuel level ran too low (fuel sloshing away from the pump)
Weak fuel pump
Clogged fuel filter or pump strainer
Faulty fuel level sender reading wrong

checks: Fill the tank and see if the misfire goes away
If it returns with a full tank, check fuel pressure and look for other misfire codes
fix: Often fixed by keeping more fuel in the tank; if it comes back with a full tank, the fuel pump or ignition parts need checking.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing, or the engine is shaking hard or losing power: ease off the gas, avoid hard acceleration and heavy loads, and get off the road and have it checked right away. Driving on a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and can leave you without power in traffic.

title: Single Cylinder Misfire (Cylinder not Specified)
plain: The computer detected that one cylinder is misfiring but can't tell which one. It is treated much like any other misfire code.
symptoms: Check engine light on, possibly flashing
Rough idle or shaking
Hesitation when accelerating

causes.name: Worn spark plug
Failing ignition coil or plug wire
Faulty or clogged fuel injector
Low compression in one cylinder

checks: Use a scan tool's misfire counters to find which cylinder is acting up
Inspect plugs and swap coils to see if the problem follows
fix: Find the weak cylinder, then usually replace its spark plug or coil.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing, or the engine is shaking hard or losing power: ease off the gas, avoid hard acceleration and heavy loads, and get off the road and have it checked right away. Driving on a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and can leave you without power in traffic.

title: Crankshaft Position System Variation Not Learned
plain: The engine computer hasn't learned the small differences in the crankshaft sensor's signal that it needs to detect misfires accurately. This often happens after the sensor or computer is replaced.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives
Misfire monitoring may not run, so the car can fail an emissions test

causes.name: Crankshaft variation relearn not done after replacing the crank sensor, engine computer or engine
Relearn procedure was attempted but did not finish
Faulty crankshaft position sensor or damaged reluctor wheel

checks: Ask whether the crank sensor or computer was recently replaced
Have a shop run the crankshaft variation relearn with a scan tool
fix: A shop runs the crank position variation relearn with a capable scan tool; no parts are usually needed.
examples: Mostly seen on GM vehicles after crank sensor or engine computer replacement

title: Misfire Detected On Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)
plain: The engine misfired in the first few seconds after starting, before it had warmed up. Moisture, a weak coil or a leaking injector are typical reasons.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Rough or shaky running right after a cold start
Rough start that smooths out after a minute

causes.name: Worn spark plugs or weak ignition coils
Moisture or coolant getting into a cylinder
Leaking or sticking fuel injector
Low fuel pressure at startup

checks: Check for single-cylinder misfire codes stored alongside it
Inspect plugs for signs of coolant or oil
Watch for coolant loss, which can point to a head gasket
fix: Usually spark plugs and/or coils; coolant in a cylinder means a deeper repair such as a head gasket.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing, or the engine is shaking hard or losing power: ease off the gas, avoid hard acceleration and heavy loads, and get off the road and have it checked right away. Driving on a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and can leave you without power in traffic.

title: Rough Road Hardware Not Present
plain: The engine computer expects to get rough-road information (used to ignore bumps that look like misfires) but can't find the part or module that supplies it.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no driving symptoms
Possible false misfire codes on bumpy roads

causes.name: Engine computer or ABS module programmed with the wrong configuration
Rough road sensor or ABS module not communicating
Wrong replacement module installed

checks: Check if a computer or ABS module was recently replaced or reprogrammed
Scan for communication codes from the ABS module
fix: Usually reprogramming the engine or ABS module so their configuration matches the vehicle.

title: Rough Road Sensor A Signal Circuit
plain: There's a problem with the signal from rough road sensor A, which helps the computer tell bumpy-road shaking apart from real misfires.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives
Possible false misfire codes on rough roads

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector at the rough road sensor
Failed rough road sensor
ABS module not supplying rough road data

checks: Inspect the sensor's wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check the ABS system for its own trouble codes
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the rough road sensor, depending on what testing shows.

title: Rough Road Sensor B Signal Circuit
plain: There's a problem with the signal from rough road sensor B, which helps the computer tell bumpy-road shaking apart from real misfires.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Usually no change in how the car drives
Possible false misfire codes on rough roads

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector at the rough road sensor
Failed rough road sensor
ABS module not supplying rough road data

checks: Inspect the sensor's wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check the ABS system for its own trouble codes
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the rough road sensor, depending on what testing shows.

title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit
plain: There's a fault with the engine speed (RPM) signal that comes from the distributor or ignition system. Without it, the computer can't time spark and fuel properly.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine stalls, cuts out or won't start
Tachometer may jump around or drop to zero

causes.name: Faulty crankshaft position or distributor pickup sensor
Bad ignition module or igniter
Damaged wiring or loose connector in the signal circuit
Worn distributor shaft bushings causing an erratic signal

checks: Check whether the tachometer works while cranking
Inspect wiring and connectors at the distributor or crank sensor
Test the pickup sensor signal with a scope or meter
fix: Usually a new crank or distributor pickup sensor, ignition module, or a wiring repair.

title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The engine speed (RPM) signal from the distributor or ignition system is erratic or doesn't match what the computer expects.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine stalls, cuts out or won't start
Tachometer may jump around or drop to zero

causes.name: Faulty crankshaft position or distributor pickup sensor
Bad ignition module or igniter
Damaged wiring or loose connector in the signal circuit
Worn distributor shaft bushings causing an erratic signal

checks: Check whether the tachometer works while cranking
Inspect wiring and connectors at the distributor or crank sensor
Test the pickup sensor signal with a scope or meter
fix: Usually a new crank or distributor pickup sensor, ignition module, or a wiring repair.

title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit No Signal
plain: The computer isn't getting any engine speed (RPM) signal from the distributor or ignition system. The engine may not start at all.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine stalls, cuts out or won't start
Tachometer may jump around or drop to zero

causes.name: Faulty crankshaft position or distributor pickup sensor
Bad ignition module or igniter
Damaged wiring or loose connector in the signal circuit
Worn distributor shaft bushings causing an erratic signal

checks: Check whether the tachometer works while cranking
Inspect wiring and connectors at the distributor or crank sensor
Test the pickup sensor signal with a scope or meter
fix: Usually a new crank or distributor pickup sensor, ignition module, or a wiring repair.

title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit Intermittent
plain: The engine speed (RPM) signal from the distributor or ignition system keeps dropping in and out, which can make the engine cut out.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Engine stalls, cuts out or won't start
Tachometer may jump around or drop to zero

causes.name: Faulty crankshaft position or distributor pickup sensor
Bad ignition module or igniter
Damaged wiring or loose connector in the signal circuit
Worn distributor shaft bushings causing an erratic signal

checks: Check whether the tachometer works while cranking
Inspect wiring and connectors at the distributor or crank sensor
Test the pickup sensor signal with a scope or meter
fix: Usually a new crank or distributor pickup sensor, ignition module, or a wiring repair.

title: Knock Control System Error
plain: The computer's system for listening for engine knock (pinging) isn't working right, so it may pull back spark timing to stay safe, which costs some power and mileage.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Slightly less power or worse fuel economy
Possible pinging on hard acceleration

causes.name: Faulty knock sensor
Damaged or corroded knock sensor wiring
